[Previous context: The 1963 earthquake killed more than 1,000 people and damaged 80% of the building stock in

Skopje.] The Project Development Objective is to help increase access of homeowners, farmers, the enterprise sector and
government agencies to financial protection from losses caused by climate change and geological hazards.
The program will support Southeast Europe and Caucasus (SEEC) countries' efforts to join Europa Re by financing their
membership contributions to the Facility. Europa Re, in turn, will facilitate the growth of catastrophe risk insurance markets
in the member countries. For the program's first phase, this component will be financed by IBRD loans (for Serbia and
FYR Macedonia) and IDA credits (for Bosnia and Herzegovina and Georgia). The SEEC CRIF will also work on building
the technical capacities through a grant, financed by donor funds and a GEF grant and implemented by Europa Re, which
includes: (i) risk mapping and modelling for participating countries; (ii) design and pricing of appropriate catastrophe risk
insurance products; (iii) small weather monitoring stations to support parametric weather insurance; and (iv) technical
assistance for regulatory and policy reforms to create an enabling market environment.
